name: loop-bounds
title: Loops with variable bounds
summary: A water-intake tracker whose glasses come from two loops bounded by host variables: filled glasses from 0 to min(drunk, goal), empty outlines from drunk to goal; an empty range simply draws nothing.
prompt: A water tracker widget: a row of glasses for a daily goal of 8, the 5 already drunk filled blue and the rest as outlines, "5 of 8 glasses", a progress bar and "3 to go".
teaches: Repeat a drawing a variable number of times: loop until "min(@drunk, @goal)" (an expression bound is re-read whenever the variable changes)
Start a second loop where the first stopped (from "@drunk" until "@goal") to draw the remainder in another style
Rely on empty ranges instead of if: when from >= until the loop body never runs (0 drunk: no filled glasses; goal reached: no outlines)
pitfalls: Clamp a bound that can exceed the space you drew for: min(@drunk, @goal) keeps a ninth glass off the row
Set the paint before the loop when every iteration shares it; a paint inside the body is re-applied on every iteration
The index is a float: from "@drunk" = 4.5 gives 4.5, 5.5, …; floor the bound if the variable can be fractional

Space loop items by a pitch derived from the width and the item count, g = (componentWidth() - 40) / @goal, rather than a literal 40: a fixed pitch overflows a narrow host and leaves a gap on a wide one

snippets.note: filled glasses: loop i from 0 until min(@drunk, @goal)

goal.meaning: daily goal in glasses (8 fit the row)

check.describe: Five filled glasses then three outlines, "5 of 8 glasses", the bar at 62 %, "3 to go". drunk 0 gives eight outlines; drunk 9 gives eight filled glasses and "0 to go". Resized (narrow 240, wide 540) the row of glasses spans the canvas: the pitch is g = (componentWidth() - 40) / @goal and each glass is gw = min(28, 0.7 g) wide, so the goal's glasses always fill the row; the bar and the count follow the width.
